meta.name: SENSE+ Pastel Companion Design System

app.name: SENSE+
app.summary: Assistive and safety companion for people with disabilities. A User side (fall detection with a three-level safety system, voice commands, Communication board, Visual Assist OCR, Hearing Assist sound alerts and captions) and a Guardian side (live status, location, battery and alerts).
app.platform: Android, Java (NOT Kotlin), XML View layouts (NOT Jetpack Compose)

meta.intendedReader: A Claude Code session that already has the SENSE+ repository open. This file is the single source of truth for the visual redesign.
meta.referenceImage: Three phone mockups of a pastel mental-health app: (1) 'Buy Sessions' screen with a large lavender plush blob character, a scalloped orange badge, a wave slider and a big orange cart button; (2) 'Mental Help' screen with a grainy cream-to-orange gradient, a SEARCH pill, and a tilted white question card stacked on ghost cards; (3) 'Hello, Samantha' home with circular icon buttons, an organic orange hero card with a yellow star character, a peeking lavender card, and soft stat tiles (Weekly Mood, Energy 80, Stress 67).
companionFiles: duck_kit.zip (33 duck VectorDrawables + looks.json + previews; unzip res/drawable/* into app/src/main/res/drawable)
meta.characterStyleReference: design/reference/duck_style_reference.jpg — the user's sticker sheet of cute white ducklings. Pip must look like those ducks.

changelog.1.1.0: Characters changed from a family of pastel blob creatures to ONE mascot, Pip the duckling, in the style of the user's duck sticker sheet. Each section now gets a Pip LOOK (outfit/prop/pose). Ducks are flat sticker art with no grain. Asset kit replaced (duck_kit.zip).

meta.goal: Re-skin every SENSE+ screen in this soft, grainy, pastel style with Pip the duckling as the mascot while keeping all behaviour intact and keeping the app fully accessible for blind, deaf, non-speaking, mobility-impaired and cognitively impaired users.

readOrder: implementationContract (hard rules: what you must and must not change)
designPrinciples + tokens (colours, type, spacing, radius, shadow, grain, motion)
characters (Pip the duckling: style, looks, expressions and the section-to-look contract)
screens (section-by-section specification; implement each screen exactly as specified)
referenceAssets (the verified duck drawable kit and look recipes)
conflictResolutionOrder: 1. Safety semantics (an emergency must always look and sound like an emergency)
2. Accessibility requirements (contrast, touch size, TalkBack, font scaling, reduced motion)
3. implementationContract rules (no behaviour changes, preserve view IDs)
4. The screen spec in this profile
5. The tokens and component specs in this profile
6. The reference image's look and feel
howToUseThisProfile.whenSomethingIsUnspecified: Derive it from the nearest component or screen spec and the designPrinciples. Never invent a new colour, font size or radius outside the tokens. Record the decision in DESIGN_NOTES.md at the repo root.

terminology.section: One functional area of the app, normally one Activity: Home, SENSE GUARD (User), Guardian, Communication, Visual Assist, Hearing Assist, Sensor Info, and the planned Navigation, Profile/Settings, Onboarding.
terminology.character: Pip, the app's single mascot: a cute white duckling in the style of the user's duck sticker sheet, drawn as layered VectorDrawables.
terminology.look: Pip dressed for one section: outfit, props and pose that show what the section does (e.g. sound waves for Hearing).
terminology.signature prop: The prop or pose inside a look that tells you which section it is (e.g. the wing raised to listen plus sound waves for Hearing).
terminology.grain: Fine monochrome noise speckle drawn over coloured UI surfaces to create the reference's soft, risograph texture. Never drawn on Pip.

mustDo: Implement every section listed in 'screens' so it matches its spec: layout order, components, tokens, character, states and copy. Visual conformance is checked section by section against this file.

Show Pip in each section's own LOOK exactly as assigned in characters.sectionCharacterContract. The look must visibly represent what the section does (Hearing -> wing raised to listen + sound waves, Visual -> round glasses + book, Communication -> speech bubble, SENSE GUARD -> superhero cape + shield with a heart, Guardian -> parent duck with a duckling, Sensor Info -> antenna headband, Navigation -> bucket hat + satchel).
Match Pip to the user's duck sticker sheet (design/reference/duck_style_reference.jpg): chubby white duckling, warm dark outline, orange beak and feet, pink blush, tiny curly tuft, flat colours.

Drive Pip's expression from the section's real state (characters.sectionCharacterContract.stateMapping), e.g. SENSE GUARD: OFF -> sleep look, NORMAL -> idle, ATTENTION -> alert + '?', EMERGENCY -> concerned + '!'.

Use only tokens defined in this profile (put them in res/values/colors.xml, dimens.xml, styles). No hard-coded hex colours in layouts or Java after the redesign; Java must use ContextCompat.getColor(ctx, R.color.token_name).
Keep the app 100% usable with TalkBack, at 200% font scale, with animations turned off, and in sunlight (contrast).
Build and run on the physical test phone after each screen; take a screenshot; tick that screen's acceptance criteria.
Write Java (not Kotlin) and XML Views (not Compose).
mustNotDo: Do not change business logic: fall detection (FallDetector, thresholds, timers), UserMonitorService state machine, voice keyword handling, Firebase/CloudHelper reads and writes, polling intervals, GuardianService notification logic, sound classification thresholds, TTS phrases that the services speak.

Do not rename, delete or change the type of any view ID that Java code looks up (see preservedViewIds). If a view must change type (e.g. TextView -> ImageView), update the Java in the same change and note it in DESIGN_NOTES.md.

Do not add heavy UI dependencies (no Lottie, Compose, Glide, image-loading or animation libraries). Everything here is achievable with the Android framework, AndroidX and Material Components already in the project.
Do not use raster images (PNG/JPG/WebP) for Pip or icons. Pip is the layered VectorDrawable kit; icons are vector drawables. The reference images are for looking at only and must not ship in the APK.
Do not put grain on Pip, text, icons, white cards, or camera previews.
Do not let Pip cover text, controls, or a control's touch area.
Do not use happy, wink or talk expressions or pastel-only styling during ATTENTION or EMERGENCY states.
Do not use the plain look as a section hero, and do not invent new mascots: every section uses Pip in its own look.
allowedPresentationChangesInJava: Replace getWindow().setStatusBarColor(...) calls with the edge-to-edge helper (androidImplementation.edgeToEdge).

Replace hard-coded Color.parseColor(...) values in UI code (MainActivity.updateStatusUi, GuardianActivity.colorFor, HearingActivity.SoundType + showIdleCard, CommunicationActivity button colours) with token colours.
Change text formatting written into views when the new layout already shows a label (e.g. tvGBattery shows '80%' instead of 'Battery: 80%').
Swap dynamically created Buttons for inflated styled item layouts (CommunicationActivity phrases).
Add calls that set character expressions, badge text, level indicator position, selected states and animations.
Replace setAlpha-based selected styling with setSelected(...) plus selector drawables.

preservedViewIds._note: Source of truth is `findViewById(R.id.` in each Activity. Re-grep before editing a layout. Known IDs at time of writing:
CommunicationActivity / activity_communi: phraseContainer (Java casts it to LinearLayout today; update the cast if you change its type)

dynamicStyleHooks.MainActivity.updateStatusUi(status, info: Single place that must apply StatusStyle (hero background, Pip look/expression/effect, badge copy, level indicator, tvStatus colour). stopMonitoring() applies StatusStyle.OFF.
dynamicStyleHooks.GuardianActivity.colorFor(status) / rend: Apply StatusStyle to the status hero card, Pip (guardian look) expression/effect and text colours.
dynamicStyleHooks.HearingActivity.onSoundDetected / showId: Apply SoundStyle (urgent vs soft), Pip (hearing look) expression + soundTypeBadge, segmented control selected state.
dynamicStyleHooks.CommunicationActivity phrase creation lo: Inflate item_phrase.xml; HELP phrase uses the emergency style.
dynamicStyleHooks.VisualAssistActivity text callback: Pip (visual look): new text -> alert (1.5 s) then idle; reading aloud -> talk.

definitionOfDone: Every screen in 'screens' with status 'existing' is implemented and passes its acceptanceCriteria.
Pip renders in every existing section's look, matches the duck reference style, animates (idle breathe + blink) and switches expressions from real state.
qa.globalChecklist passes (build, TalkBack, 200% font, reduced motion, contrast, no behaviour regressions in the testing checklist).
DESIGN_NOTES.md lists every deviation from this profile with a reason.

referenceAnalysis.overallMood: Soft, warm, tactile and friendly. Pastel lavender and tangerine/peach dominate, with butter yellow accents. Colour surfaces have fine grain like risograph paper or felt. Plush 3D-ish blob characters with tiny faces give emotional warmth. Lots of white space, big rounded shapes, and few but confident type sizes.

elements: White pill button with arrow + 'BACK' in small bold caps; screen title right-aligned in bold.
Top ~55% is a lavender hero area with a giant purple plush blob creature (bunny-like lumps on top) cropped by the right edge; tiny face with dot eyes, small smile and pink blush.
Scalloped (flower/cookie-edged) orange badge with a small medallion on top, holding short centred text.
Hero area ends in a soft wave; below it a pill slider track with a lavender-to-orange gradient and a grip thumb.
Number row (3 4 5 6 7 8 9) with the selected value large, orange, with a dot above and a caption ('Days') below.
Bottom: 'Total' label and a huge bold '59$'; a large orange stadium button with a cart icon on the right.
screen1_buySessions.mapsTo: SENSE GUARD (User) screen: lavender hero with a big Pip in the guard look, scalloped status badge, wave + safety-level indicator (Normal/Attention/Emergency instead of days), big primary action.

elements: Full-bleed grainy gradient: pale cream-yellow top-left through peach to saturated orange on the right, fading to white near the bottom.
White pill SEARCH button left, white circular settings button right.

A white card tilted a few degrees, with two translucent ghost cards stacked behind/above it (deck effect). Card: author row with avatar and role, big centred question text, a meta row ('23 Minutes' —— '1.2K Users'), then two small circular action buttons.
Bottom navigation with three line icons, the active one orange, on a white bar with a gentle centre bump.
screen2_mentalHelp.mapsTo: Hearing Assist: grainy peach gradient background, Pip (hearing look) above a tilted alert card deck whose main card shows the detected sound.

elements: Small avatar + 'Hello,' + large bold name. Two white circular icon buttons on the right (notification with red dot, calendar).

Horizontal carousel: an organic-shaped orange gradient card ('Self Care' white chip, 'Keep your head up.' in white, round arrow button) with a grainy yellow star character cropped at the bottom-left; the next lavender card peeks in from the right edge.
Section heading 'Your week at a glance'.

Soft cream tiles: 'Weekly Mood' with a grainy pastel semicircle chart, 'Calm' and a 'TOP MOOD' chip; 'Energy' and 'Stress' tiles with a small arrow chip and big LIGHT-weight numbers (80, 67); tiny status dots (green/red).
Bottom: a floating circular hamburger button sitting in a notch of the bottom bar.
screen3_home.mapsTo: Home: greeting, hero carousel for SENSE GUARD and Guardian, tool tiles for the assist sections. Guardian dashboard: stat tiles with big light numbers.

traitsToKeep: Grainy pastel gradients on coloured surfaces; crisp white cards on top.
A big character bleeding off an edge for depth and charm (in SENSE+ this is Pip, in the duck sticker style).
Pill and circular white controls with very soft shadows.
Organic shapes: scallops, waves, slightly asymmetric card edges, tilted card decks.
Big numbers in LIGHT weight; titles in BOLD; tiny caps labels with wide letter spacing.
traitsToAdaptForAccessibility: White text on light orange in the reference fails contrast; SENSE+ uses ink text on pastel and vivid fills, and white text only on 700+ shades or emergency red.
Reference caps labels are about 10sp; SENSE+ minimum is 12sp, body minimum 16sp.
Reference icon buttons are about 40dp; SENSE+ minimum touch target is 48dp (primary actions 64dp+).
Pastel is never the only signal for alerts: urgent states use saturated colour, text, icon, motion and vibration together.

designPrinciples.name: Soft but legible
designPrinciples.rule: Pastel atmosphere, but every piece of text and every control meets WCAG 2.2 AA.

designPrinciples.name: One hero per screen
designPrinciples.rule: Each screen has exactly one dominant visual (usually the section character on a gradient). Everything else is calm white cards.

designPrinciples.name: Pip tells you where you are
designPrinciples.rule: A user who cannot read well should recognise the section from Pip's look and the section colour alone.

designPrinciples.name: Emotion follows state
designPrinciples.rule: Pip reacts to real app state and never contradicts it (no smiling during an emergency).

designPrinciples.name: Big targets, few choices
designPrinciples.rule: Primary actions are large (64dp+), secondary actions are clearly secondary, and no screen has more than one primary action.

designPrinciples.name: Emergency overrides aesthetics
designPrinciples.rule: ATTENTION and EMERGENCY use saturated, high-contrast styling, motion and haptics, no matter how pastel the rest is.

designPrinciples.name: Texture on colour only
designPrinciples.rule: Grain on coloured UI surfaces only; Pip (flat sticker art), text, icons and white cards stay clean.

designPrinciples.name: Sticker clarity
designPrinciples.rule: Pip is flat sticker art with one warm outline, like the duck reference; UI surfaces carry the softness (gradients, grain, soft shadows).

designPrinciples.name: Calm motion
designPrinciples.rule: Slow, gentle, purposeful motion; everything still works and still makes sense with animations off.

color._naming: In colors.xml use snake_case: tangerine_500, lavender_100, ink_900, surface_canvas, status_emergency_solid, etc.
_usageRules: 50/100: large surface tints (tiles, hero backgrounds, list highlights).
200-400: character bodies, gradient stops, decorative shapes, selected fills behind ink text.
500: vivid accents (icons on white at >=3:1 for 500+ except butter/mint, gradient ends, active indicators). Never body text.
700: icons and LARGE text (>= 24sp regular or >= 19sp bold) on white or tints; white text on 700 fills is allowed.
800/900: small text on the family's 50/100 tint (>= 4.5:1).
Text on any pastel or vivid fill (200-500) is ink_900. White text only on 700+ fills, emergency/urgent solids, or dark gradients verified at >= 4.5:1 under the text.

ink_900.use: Headings, primary text, text on pastel/vivid fills

ink_500.use: Captions, caps labels, inactive labels (lowest allowed text colour)

ink_400.use: Disabled text and decorative only — NEVER informative text (2.87:1)

surface_card.use: Cards, sheets, pill buttons, circular buttons

surface_glass.use: Translucent white chips and arrow buttons on gradients

surface_ghostCard1.use: First ghost card in a card deck

surface_ghostCard2.use: Second ghost card in a card deck

sectionAccents._rule: Each section owns one palette family. Its character, hero gradient, tile tint and selected states use that family.

soundTypes._rule: Urgent sounds (flash=true in HearingActivity.SoundType) use the solid style: card background = solid, all text white (>= 4.5:1). Non-urgent sounds keep a white card with a tinted icon tile and ink text.

gradients._implementation: Linear gradients: <shape><gradient android:angle .../></shape> XML. Multi-blob 'mesh' gradients: HeroBackgroundDrawable (Java) layering 2-3 RadialGradient shaders over a base colour, then grain. Coordinates are fractions of the drawable bounds.

grad_hero_lavender.use: SENSE GUARD normal, Guardian, Home avatar

grad_hero_butter.use: SENSE GUARD attention, Visual Assist header

grad_hero_emergency.rule: Lighter blob only behind the character, never behind text. Text sits on the #D92D20 base (white 4.83:1).
grad_hero_emergency.use: SENSE GUARD emergency, Guardian emergency card

fontFamily.primary: Lexend (Google Fonts, SIL Open Font License). Chosen because it is geometric and soft like the reference AND designed for reading proficiency, which suits cognitive and low-vision users.
fontFamily.alternate: Outfit (closest match to the reference) if Lexend is rejected.
fontFamily.fallback: sans-serif (Roboto) with the same sizes and weights.
fontFamily.howToGet: Download the family zip from fonts.google.com/specimen/Lexend and copy the STATIC instances (static/ folder) into app/src/main/res/font, renaming to lowercase_with_underscores. If the session cannot download, ask the user to drop the files in and use the fallback until then.
fontFamily.referencingRule: Reference the weight file directly (android:fontFamily="@font/lexend_semibold") instead of relying on android:textFontWeight, which only works on API 28+ (minSdk is 26).

scale._note: Final sizes already include a +15% accessibility uplift over the reference. All sizes in sp. Never set text sizes in dp. referencePx = approximate size in the mockup.

headline_l.use: Greeting name, screen titles on hero

title_m.use: Tile titles, top-bar titles, section headers

body_m.use: Default body (minimum size for meaningful text)

label_caps.use: BACK, chips, tile labels in caps

typography.androidStyles: Create TextAppearance.SENSE.<Name> styles for every scale entry in res/values/styles_text.xml and reference them with android:textAppearance. Use includeFontPadding=false on display/headline styles for tight vertical rhythm, and keep it true for body text.
rules: Max 2 weights per card (e.g. semibold title + regular body).
Big numbers use LIGHT weight; never bold large numbers except display_numberBold.
Left-align body text; centre only short titles (<= 3 lines) on cards and heroes.
Use real sentence case in copy; caps only through label_caps/caption_caps styles.

elevation._android: Use elevation + outline shadow colours (android:outlineSpotShadowColor / outlineAmbientShadowColor, API 28+, ignored on 26-27). Set theme attrs android:spotShadowAlpha=0.14 and android:ambientShadowAlpha=0.06 for the soft look. White cards need a non-transparent background for the outline shadow to render.

glow_tangerine.fallbackApi26_27: bg_glow_tangerine.xml: oval radial gradient #66F7893B -> #00F7893B, 24dp larger than the button, offset 8dp down, placed behind it

grain.description: Fine speckle noise reproducing the UI reference's grainy gradients. Used on coloured surfaces only.

texture.format: ARGB_8888, generated once at runtime and cached statically
texture.scale: 1 texel = 1 device pixel (do not scale with density, grain must stay fine)

drawing.onShapes: Draw the shape with its gradient Paint, then draw the SAME path again with a Paint whose shader is BitmapShader(noise, REPEAT, REPEAT). This clips grain to the shape without saveLayer.
drawing.onPip: Never. Pip is flat sticker art.

patterns.pressFeedback: Scale to 0.96 over 90ms on ACTION_DOWN, back to 1.0 with playfulPop over 240ms on release. Elevation drops by 2dp while pressed. Plus HapticFeedbackConstants.VIRTUAL_KEY.
patterns.screenEnter: Hero fades in (240ms); character scales 0.92 -> 1.0 with playfulPop (360ms); cards slide up 16dp + fade, staggered 40ms each, decelerate.
patterns.characterIdle: Pip breathe: scaleX/scaleY 1.0 -> 1.025 (3200ms, reverse, infinite, pivot at bottom centre). Bob: translationY 0 -> -3dp (2400ms, reverse, infinite). Blink: swap to duck_face_sleeping for 120ms at random 3-6s intervals.
patterns.characterReact: When Pip's expression or look changes: squash 1.0 -> 0.94 (scaleY) / 1.04 (scaleX) over 90ms, then playfulPop back to 1.0 over 360ms, swapping layers at the squash peak.
patterns.soundWaves: duck_hearing_waves alpha 0.35 <-> 1.0 (1200ms, reverse, infinite) while listening; on detection hold at 1.0 for 2s.
patterns.pulseRing: Two concentric rings expand 1.0 -> 1.6 and fade 0.5 -> 0 over pulsePeriod, offset half a period. Period >= 800ms (photosensitivity rule: never more than 3 flashes per second).
patterns.stateCrossfade: Background colours animate with ValueAnimator.ofArgb over 360ms; hero gradients crossfade with TransitionDrawable(360ms).
patterns.numberCountUp: Stat numbers count from previous to new value over 600ms (decelerate) only when the change is > 0.
patterns.levelIndicator: Thumb translationX animates to the active level over 360ms (standard).

reducedMotion.detect: !ValueAnimator.areAnimatorsEnabled() (API 26+) — true when the user turned animations off.
reducedMotion.behaviour: No idle loops, no pulse rings (show a static 2dp ring instead), no count-up, no card tilt animation (keep static tilt), state changes are instant. Blink is disabled. Information must never depend on motion.

iconography.style: Material Symbols Rounded, weight 400, grade 0, optical size 24. Outline for inactive, FILL=1 for active/selected.
iconography.colour: ink_800 on white; ink_900 on pastel fills; white on solid status colours; section 700 shade for accent icons.
iconography.source: Android Studio > New > Vector Asset > Clip Art (Material Icons Rounded), or Material Symbols SVGs imported as vectors. Name them ic_<name>.xml.

touchTargets.rule: If the visual is smaller than 48dp (e.g. arrow chip), extend the touch area with padding or TouchDelegate.

layout.grid: 2 columns on phones with 14dp gap; 3 columns when width >= 600dp.
layout.verticalRhythm: Top bar -> hero -> section header -> content, separated by gapBetweenSections (28dp).

characters.summary: SENSE+ has ONE mascot: Pip, a chubby white baby duckling drawn in the hand-drawn kawaii sticker style of the user's duck reference sheet. Every section shows Pip in that section's own LOOK (outfit + props + pose), and Pip's face reacts to the section's real state. Name is a suggestion; renaming it is only a copy change.

styleReferenceImage.authority: This image is the style authority for Pip. If this text and the image disagree about how Pip LOOKS, follow the image. This profile still decides structure, section mapping, accessibility and implementation.
styleReferenceImage.whatItShows: A sticker sheet of 11 chubby white ducklings on a cream background, each doing something different, with small doodles around them (hearts, sparkles, music note, Z's, motion lines, water splashes, grass and flowers).

posesAndHowWeUseThem.pose: Waving one wing, open happy beak, floating pink heart, motion marks
Hugging a big pink heart, winking
posesAndHowWeUseThem.use: optional 'thanks' look (e.g. Communication 'Thank you' phrase art, Guardian empty state)

posesAndHowWeUseThem.pose: Yellow bucket hat and a yellow cross-body satchel
posesAndHowWeUseThem.use: nav look for the planned Navigation section (built)

posesAndHowWeUseThem.pose: Reading a blue book, music note floating
posesAndHowWeUseThem.use: visual look, with round glasses added so it reads as 'seeing' (built)

posesAndHowWeUseThem.pose: Splashing in water with a rubber-duck bag
Sleeping in bed with a blue polka-dot nightcap and blanket, 'Z z z'
posesAndHowWeUseThem.use: sleep look = feature switched off (built as nightcap + Z's; the full bed scene is optional for the SENSE GUARD OFF hero)

posesAndHowWeUseThem.pose: Holding a flower, wearing an orange bow tie
posesAndHowWeUseThem.use: profile look for the planned Profile/Settings section
optional phrase art for 'I need water / a drink'

posesAndHowWeUseThem.pose: Wearing a green dinosaur costume, sparkles

styleGuide.rendering: Flat vector sticker art: solid fills, one warm dark outline, flat cel-shading shapes. NO gradients and NO grain on Pip (grain stays on UI surfaces only).
styleGuide.silhouette: One continuous outline for head and body (no neck line). Big round head about 120 units wide on the 240-unit canvas; round sitting body about 150 units wide at the bottom; a small soft tail bump at the lower right; a tiny two-bump curly tuft on top of the head. Whole duck about 206 units tall x 158 units wide, standing on y=222.
styleGuide.proportions: Chibi: the head is about half of the total height. The face sits in the lower half of the head. Eyes are tiny and far apart; the beak is wide and flat.

outline.style: round caps and round joins; constant width; wings are drawn with an OPEN outline stroke on their outer edge only, so they look like flaps on the body

colours.bodyShade: #EEEAF0 flat crescent in the lower right of the body, clipped to the silhouette; #F4F1F5 faint band on the right side of the head
colours.eyes: #2B2523 with a white 1.5-unit shine at the upper right
colours.blush: #FFB3BA at 85% opacity, flat oval 19 x 12 units, no outline
colours.groundShadow: #2B2633 at 10% opacity, flat ellipse 140 x 16 units under the feet (works on any background, including red)

faceLayout._units: 240-unit canvas, same for every look so faces never move between looks
faceLayout.beak: centred at (120,106), 34 wide x 18 tall, rounded flat bill with a smile line

styleGuide.wings: Small rounded flaps. Poses: down (resting at the sides), wave (left wing raised + two motion marks), listen (right wing raised beside the head), hold (both wings in front, drawn OVER the held prop).
styleGuide.feet: Two orange rounded webbed feet poking forward at the bottom, each with two toe bumps, outlined.
styleGuide.doodles: Small decorations around Pip, drawn flat (hearts, sparkles, music notes, Z's, motion marks, '?' and '!' bubbles). They are separate layers so they can animate or be hidden at small sizes.
styleGuide.personality: Gentle, helpful, a little shy and always kind. Never scary, never sarcastic, never mocking.
donts: No realistic or adult duck features (no long neck, no coloured head feathers, no teeth).
No sketchy or broken lines; no pure black.
No gradients, grain, glows or drop shadows on Pip (only the flat ground ellipse).
Do not move or resize the face between looks; all looks share duck_base.
No text inside props except the '?' and '!' glyph bubbles.
Never show happy, wink or talk expressions during ATTENTION or EMERGENCY.

expressions._files: Each expression is one VectorDrawable on the same 240-unit canvas: duck_face_<name>.xml
expressions.idle: Dot eyes with shine, closed beak with a small smile line. Default.
expressions.happy: Closed '^ ^' eyes, open beak with tongue. Success, greeting, all clear.
expressions.wink: One dot eye, one '>' wink, open beak. Celebrations and tips.
expressions.talk: Dot eyes, open beak. Alternate with idle every 150ms while text-to-speech is speaking.
expressions.alert: Slightly bigger eyes, small open beak. Attention, something detected, listening hard.
expressions.concerned: Small eyes, worried brows, downturned beak line, sweat drop. Emergency, errors, missing permission.
expressions.sleeping: Closed '‿ ‿' eyes, closed beak. Feature off or paused. Also used as the 120ms blink frame.

looks._recipe: Ordered layer lists (bottom to top). FACE = the current expression's face drawable. FX = the current effect layer (question/exclaim/sparkles), if any. PARENT[...] = layers drawn with the parent transform (translate 40,33; scale 0.84; in canvas units). The same data is in duck_kit/looks.json.

home.means: Hello! Waving with a floating heart.

guard.means: Little superhero: orange cape and a lavender shield with a heart = protection + care.

guardian.means: A parent duck watching over a small duckling = the guardian looking after someone.

comm.means: Waving with a speech bubble = speaks for the user.

visual.means: Round glasses + reading a book = sees and reads text aloud.

hearing.means: Wing raised beside the head + sound waves = listens for the user.

sensor.means: Antenna headband with a signal = senses things.

nav.means: Explorer bucket hat + satchel (straight from the reference) = finds the way.

plain.means: Neutral fallback, e.g. the debug gallery.

profile_planned.layers: plain + a bow-tie layer (orange, like the reference) + a held flower in the wave pose
profile_planned.means: Dressed up = your profile and preferences.

cognitive_planned.layers: hold pose + a small notebook with a pencil

sectionCharacterContract._rule: Mandatory. Every section's hero is Pip in THAT section's look. The look must show what the section does through its outfit/prop/pose, and Pip's expression must follow the section's real state. A reviewer must be able to tell which section a screenshot is from by looking at Pip alone. Never use the plain look as a section hero.
sectionCharacterContract.senseGuard: guard look (sleep look while monitoring is OFF)

hearingAssist.sound detected: alert, waves at full opacity, + soundTypeBadge chip next to Pip

processForNewSections: Design a new LOOK for Pip, not a new character.
1. Write the section's job in one sentence.
2. Choose ONE outfit, prop or pose that shows that job (use the reference sheet's poses first).
3. Colour the prop from the section's palette family; keep Pip white with the standard outline.
4. Draw the prop as separate layer(s) on the 240-unit canvas, aligned to duck_base, with the outline style above.
5. Add the recipe to looks.json and DuckLooks.java, and its state mapping here.
6. Check it in the debug gallery against characters.qaChecklist.

placementRules.canvas: Every look is a square 240-unit canvas; DuckView keeps the aspect ratio and anchors to the bottom centre.
placementRules.backdrop: Pip is white. On white cards, always place a family_100 circle or soft blob behind Pip (part of the layout, not the duck). On tinted or gradient surfaces no backdrop is needed.
placementRules.hero: 220-260dp. May be cropped up to 15% by the right or bottom edge, but never the face or the look's prop.
placementRules.card: 130-160dp, bottom-left or bottom-right, clipped by the card.
placementRules.peek: 110-130dp overlapping a card edge (Visual Assist camera card, Hearing deck).
placementRules.avatar: Head only: draw the look into a 44dp circle, scaled so the top 55% of the canvas fills it.
placementRules.smallSizes: Below 64dp hide optional doodle layers (notes, sparkles, hearts) so Pip stays readable. Minimum 40dp.
placementRules.mirroring: Allowed (scaleX -1) so Pip faces the content, but draw '?'/'!' bubbles un-mirrored.

implementation.assets: duck_kit.zip -> res/drawable/duck_*.xml: 33 VectorDrawables, all 240 x 240 viewport, perfectly aligned. Uses only paths, strokes, fills with alpha, groups with translate/scale and clip-path: all supported from API 21.

publicApi: void setEffect(Effect e) // NONE, QUESTION, EXCLAIM, SPARKLES
ui/DuckView.java.draw: k = min(w, h) / 240f. Translate so the canvas is bottom-centred. For each layer: drawable.setBounds(0, 0, 240k, 240k); drawable.draw(canvas). For PARENT layers: canvas.save(); canvas.translate(40k, 33k); canvas.scale(0.84f, 0.84f); draw; canvas.restore(). Resolve drawables once per look/expression change (ContextCompat.getDrawable(...).mutate()), never in onDraw.
ui/DuckView.java.animation: Idle breathe/bob on the whole canvas (pivot bottom centre). Blink: swap FACE to duck_face_sleeping for 120ms every 3-6s when the expression has open eyes. Talk: alternate duck_face_talk and duck_face_idle every 150ms. Hearing waves: alpha 0.35 <-> 1.0 over 1200ms. React: squash and pop on expression change. Pulse rings: drawn in code behind the duck. Pause everything when not visible; disable loops when animations are off.
ui/DuckView.java.performance: For views >= 200dp, cache the drawn stack in a bitmap per (look, expression, effect) and redraw the cached bitmap while idle-animating; invalidate the cache on change.
ui/DuckView.java.accessibility: setImportantForAccessibility(IMPORTANT_FOR_ACCESSIBILITY_NO). Whatever Pip shows must also be stated in text nearby.

classes.ui/DuckLooks.java: enum Look with the ordered layer lists from looks.json (drawable resource ids), the PARENT transform, and each look's default expression.

edgeToEdge.why: targetSdk 37 means edge-to-edge is enforced on Android 15+ (the test phone): Window.setStatusBarColor is deprecated and has no effect, and content draws behind the system bars. The current layouts fake this with paddingTop=44dp.
how: In every Activity.onCreate before setContentView: EdgeToEdge.enable(this) (androidx.activity).

Light icons on light screens: WindowCompat.getInsetsController(getWindow(), getWindow().getDecorView()).setAppearanceLightStatusBars(true) — set false while a screen shows an emergency (dark red) hero.

Insets: ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener(topBar, (v, insets) -> { Insets bars = insets.getInsets(WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars()); v.setPadding(v.getPaddingLeft(), bars.top + dp(12), v.getPaddingRight(), v.getPaddingBottom()); return insets; }) and the same for bottom content with bars.bottom.
Put this in ui/Ui.java: Ui.applyEdgeToEdge(Activity a, View top, View bottom, boolean lightIcons).

androidImplementation.materialButtonGotcha: Under a Material 3 theme every <Button> inflates as MaterialButton. A custom android:background is only used if app:backgroundTint="@null"; otherwise the tint overrides it. Prefer MaterialButton attributes (cornerRadius, backgroundTint, strokeColor/Width, icon, iconTint, iconGravity) and fall back to backgroundTint=@null + drawable only for gradients.

performance: Build gradients, paths and bitmaps in onSizeChanged/onBoundsChange, never in onDraw.
One shared grain tile (128x128 ARGB = 64 KB).
Pip cache bitmaps are sized to the view (a 260dp hero at xxhdpi is about 780x780 = 2.4 MB); release them in onDetachedFromWindow.
Pause idle animations when views are not visible (onVisibilityAggregated).
Avoid stacking full-screen backgrounds (remove windowBackground behind full-bleed heroes, or let the hero be the window background) to limit overdraw.
Use setLayerType(LAYER_TYPE_HARDWARE) only while a view is running a transform animation, then reset to NONE.
androidImplementation.testDevice: Samsung Galaxy A55 (Android 15+, One UI). Also check one small-screen emulator (360 x 640dp) and font scale 2.0.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA + Android accessibility guidelines. This is an assistive app; accessibility failures are functional bugs.

contrast.verified: Token pairs in tokens.color list measured ratios; any new pair must be checked (e.g. Accessibility Scanner app).

screenReader: Pip, ghost cards, grain, decorative chips: importantForAccessibility=no.
Screen titles and section headers: accessibilityHeading=true (ViewCompat.setAccessibilityHeading for API 26-27).
Status texts (tvStatus, tvGStatus, tvListening, alert title): accessibilityLiveRegion polite (assertive for EMERGENCY and urgent sounds).
Clickable cards: one focusable node with a merged contentDescription; inner views not focusable.
accessibility.fontScaling: All text in sp, no fixed heights on text containers (use minHeight), test at font scale 2.0 + display size largest: nothing clipped, tiles grow, deck rotation becomes 0°.
accessibility.colourIndependence: Every colour-coded state is also expressed in text and icon (and haptics where it already exists).
accessibility.motion: Respect animations-off (tokens.motion.reducedMotion). No information conveyed only by motion.
accessibility.photosensitivity: No element flashes more than 3 times per second; pulse periods >= 800ms; the existing torch blink (about 2 per second) is within limits — do not speed it up.
accessibility.cognitive: Plain language, one primary action per screen, consistent placement of Back and the primary button. Pip gives emotional context but never replaces words.

contentAndCopy.voice: Warm, calm, short, second person. Plain words. Never alarming beyond 'Possible emergency'. No emoji in UI text (characters carry the emotion); emoji stays only in system notifications that already use it.

strings.comm_sub: Tap a phrase — I'll say it out loud
strings.visual_placeholder: Point the camera at some text

vectorDrawableNotes: All files use viewport 240 x 240 and android:width/height 240dp; DuckView sets bounds, so the intrinsic size does not matter.
Cel shading uses <group><clip-path .../><path .../></group> to keep the shade inside the body outline.
The duckling and the guardian parent use <group> translate+scale (VectorDrawable applies scale, then translate, the same as SVG translate() scale()).
Stroke widths scale with the drawable, so at 48dp the outline is about 0.9dp. That is the smallest size where Pip still reads well; below 64dp hide doodle layers.
referenceAssets.grainTextureJava: static Bitmap build() { int s = 128; Bitmap b = Bitmap.createBitmap(s, s, Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888); java.util.Random r = new java.util.Random(7); int[] px = new int[s * s]; for (int i = 0; i < px.length; i++) { float p = r.nextFloat(); if (p < 0.20f) px[i] = Color.argb((int) (255 * (0.10f + r.nextFloat() * 0.12f)), 255, 255, 255); else if (p < 0.40f) px[i] = Color.argb((int) (255 * (0.05f + r.nextFloat() * 0.07f)), 40, 20, 60); else px[i] = Color.TRANSPARENT; } b.setPixels(px, 0, s, 0, 0, s, s); return b; }  // for UI surfaces only, never for Pip
